terrainOutwardNormal.detail: The authoritative terrain mesh is drawn by its BACK faces (set the material to FrontSide and the ground vanishes, leaving only the world-box side walls). three's DOUBLE_SIDED therefore flips the authored upward vertex normal and lights the ground through a downward one, which inverts every slope-dependent term. Ordinary ground hides it, because its relief comes from the baked terrainShade computed from the TRUE normal and the direct lights are a small share of an environment-dominated scene. Metal ore does not hide it: its metalness/roughness reflection is lit entirely through the normal, so a north-facing ore slope reflected and shaded as if it faced the southern sun. 'ore' restores the authored outward normal only where the ore region covers, fixing that and leaving every other pixel byte-identical. 'terrain' applies it to the whole surface - more physically correct, and a large change: the ground starts taking sky irradiance instead of floor irradiance and brightens substantially, so the biome palette and RenderLighting3D scales would want retuning. 'off' keeps the historical flipped normal for bisecting.

worldBox.detail: Water extends this far beyond every terrain edge AND this far below the world-box floor. The world-box walls descend by depthAverageAxisFraction × ((map width + map length) / 2), and both the land slab and the liquid are capped at their floor, so each is a closed solid.

presetBackdrop.detail: Four map-centered panorama shells, ordered near to terminal. Effective distance is max(minimumDistanceWorldUnits, distanceMapFactor times the larger map axis). The first three generated UASTC KTX2 textures are transparent RGBA scenery/cloud layers; terminal is the fully opaque sky and is the only layer allowed to contain stars. verticalOffsetDegrees applies to all four: 0 is authored placement, negative lowers, positive raises. Generator blur must increase with distance.

mapInfoAnnex.detail: The strip of land the map caption stands on — a headland grown straight out of the middle of the map edge BEHIND ally team 0, emitted into the terrain mesh itself so the terrain shader paints it and the liquid box grows around it. widthMapFraction (along the edge) and depthMapFraction (outward) scale against the larger map axis, so the annex keeps the same whole-map-zoom size on every map; on a long, thin map that would grow a tongue wider than the coast it hangs off, so both are scaled down together until the width fits maxEdgeSpanFraction of that edge. blendDepthFraction is how much of that depth is spent easing from the map's own edge profile to the flat table the caption stands on, as a fraction of the depth; the rest is flat. Each flank is then divided in THREE: the outer third's corner is cut away on a diagonal, and the identical triangle is added back over the inner third, flaring the headland where it meets the coast — so the annex loses a corner to open water and gains one filling the inside corner against the map's own edge, at no change in area. cornerCutSlope is how far that diagonal travels ACROSS the annex per unit of flank it covers: 1 is a 45° cut, lower is a longer shallower taper, and 0 leaves the plain rectangle. surfaceStepLandCellFraction is the annex's triangle spacing as a fraction of the land cell, so its mesh is at least as fine as the terrain it joins.

mapPresetLabel.detail: The caption standing on the flat table of the map info annex (see mapInfoAnnex), behind ally team 0. It is one centred block in three sections — the preset name (or CUSTOM), the live map's settings, and the byline — laid out the way a page would lay them out. Font sizes are canvas pixels and set the block's internal proportions; the block is then scaled to fill the annex's flat table inset by captionMarginAnnexDepthFraction × the annex depth on EVERY side, and the settings fields are wrapped across rows (and the section leading grown) until the block's aspect matches that inset table exactly — which is what makes the gap even on all four sides at the largest type the table can carry. lineGapPx is the leading between settings rows, sectionGapPx the space between sections, and ruleThicknessPx / ruleWidthInkFraction the divider between the settings and the byline (its width as a fraction of the block's ink width). canvasPadPx is the block's own padding, measured against the glyphs' own INK rather than the font box so the gap over the title matches the gap beside it. The caption stands clear of the annex's ramp off the coast only as far as the ramp actually rises: captionFlatToleranceAnnexDepthFraction × the annex depth is how much residual rise counts as flat, so a map whose edge is already at the table's altitude gives the sign the WHOLE headland. captionMinAspect is the squarest block the caption is willing to be set in: the headland tapers, so a box taken all the way to its rim comes out nearly square, and the only way a caption fills a square is by breaking its settings into a column of scraps narrower than its own title. The box is the deepest one CENTRED on the headland that still reads as a sign at that shape; everything past it stays landform. Raise it for a longer, shallower sign, lower it to push the block toward a column. The sign is RAISED, not printed: the letters are extruded geometry cut from the block's own glyph mask, with nothing drawn over them, and they always rise from the annex surface to letterReliefTitleFraction × the title font ABOVE whichever is higher, the ground they stand on or the liquid surface — so the caption reads from above the water and the letters run down through it to the bed. letterMaskSupersample is how much finer than the block's authored scale the traced mask is, and letterMaskSimplifyPx the outline simplification tolerance in mask pixels (larger = fewer triangles, blockier glyphs).

vegetationWeathering.detail: Weathering for everything that grows - world-unit bark/foliage/grass projection, soil at the base of each plant, dry patches dissolved through the live colour, and dust on upward-facing surfaces. false restores uv-space texture repeats and flat foliage; keep it as a bisect and as the lever if the extra fragment work ever matters, since vegetation is the most numerous thing in the world. Tuning lives in colorsConfig.environment.vegetationWeathering.

terrainWallWear.detail: The worn top and bottom rims of a D-PLATEAU wall. false draws the fold the mesh describes, which is the clean terrace edge this treatment replaces - keep it as a bisect. Tuning lives in colorsConfig.world.terrain.wallWear. Intensity is driven by the dihedral angle measured at each rim, so a wall flattened flush into the terrain wears nothing: the treatment must never draw a step the map author deliberately erased.

terrainOreEdge.detail: The weathered ore-to-ground transition (warped contour, granular dissolve, dirt band). false draws the region field's own contour straight, which is the clean stencilled edge this treatment replaces - keep it as a bisect. Tuning lives in colorsConfig.environment.metalDeposit.edge. A SURFACE = METAL world switches it off on its own: the whole map is ore there, so every deposit boundary is interior and a dirt band around one would be drawing a seam that does not exist.

terrainMetalGrime.detail: Dirt and grime over the metal body itself - every ore fragment, deposit interiors and SURFACE = METAL worlds included, not just the edge band. false restores clean plate everywhere the edge band does not reach - keep it as a bisect. Tuning lives in colorsConfig.environment.metalDeposit.bodyGrime. Unlike terrainOreEdge this stays ON for a SURFACE = METAL world: it needs no boundary, and an all-metal world is exactly where it is the only source of dirt.

tree.detail: textureRepeat is gone on purpose: the bark and leaf tiles are projected from world position at an authored WORLD size (colorsConfig.environment.vegetationWeathering) rather than sampled through the models' uvs. Through uvs at a fixed repeat, a big tree and a small tree wore bark at different physical sizes.

entityShadow.detail: darknessPercent is the contact shadow's OWN strength. It used to borrow fogConfig radarDarknessPercent, so changing how dark radar contacts look also changed how dark unit shadows were. 35 is that value, so the look is unchanged and the coupling is gone.
